Hi all — technical summary below (keeping it short; happy to expand into SIG evidence rows if needed):

1) Training on customer data: 
- Default: Customer prompts and generated outputs are NOT incorporated into model training pipelines. We maintain separation between customer inference traffic and datasets used for model training/fine-tuning.
- Exceptions: With explicit customer opt-in (rare, documented engagement), data can be used for research/fine-tuning under contract with clear scope, TTL, and deletion controls. Those instances are handled via separate agreements and are recorded with approvals.

2) Prompt/response retention and storage lifecycle: 
- Inference path: Requests are routed to GPU runtime; we use an in-memory KV cache for short-term prefix caching to reduce duplicate compute. The KV cache is in-memory only and not persisted to disk. Typical in-memory TTL is per-request (seconds) except when configured for session continuity.
- Operational logs: We persist auditing/telemetry logs for debugging and billing. Default retention for raw, unredacted logs is 30 days. These logs are stored encrypted-at-rest using customer-tenant encryption keys where available; by default they are encrypted with our KMS and can be integrated with customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Prompt analytics: We store token-level telemetry and anonymized usage metrics longer-term (up to 1 year) for product telemetry; PII/PHI redaction is applied where detected by our automated redaction heuristics. Customers can request reduced retention windows or opt for token-only billing records without storing plaintext prompts.

3) PHI redaction and HIPAA posture: 
- For Medicore pilot: we recommend enabling prompt redaction and configuring Dedicated or Private deployment with customer-managed KMS. We can also enable stricter retention (e.g., 7 days) for logs and disable long-term analytics for the Medicore tenant.

4) SCCs and EU transfers: 
- Redwood executes the European Commission standard contractual clauses (SCCs) for data transfers and provides a DPA that references SCCs. Our SCCs/DPA template will be included with this thread.

5) Evidence artifacts attached: SIG matrix (PDF) and a tailored data flow map for Medicore. If you need per-control artifacts (config screenshots, KMS key ids, audit entries), we can produce a scoped packet under a secure share.

If Medicore's risk committee needs an example sanitized log sample, we can provide an audited, redacted sample. Please confirm the level of sanitization required.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
